instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Warmly Withholding
cards.instruction: Remain open, caring, and reassuring while revealing less with every new question.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've crossed the dates out like the headteacher did. All arranged, love. Your suspension's taken care of. Have some tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those are the school holidays. How long am I suspended?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A little while. I'll be home with you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will I miss the school play?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Oh, sweetheart. Come sit beside me. You don't have to face this alone.

cards.title: Secrets Have Value
cards.instruction: Price every fact, introduction, warning, and confession as something that must be traded for equal value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two fingers, like yours. A name each, then. I'll name who reported you late if you name who reported me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm ordering two coffees. I only know which department.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Coffee settled. Then departments for departments. Names cost names.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Payroll. But I can introduce you to my source.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Marketing. I'll arrange coffee with mine too. Same access, same price.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put a pound beside yours. One secret each. Tell me something Mum could ground you for, then I'll explain her spare key.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My pound's for the bus. I broke her mug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fares ready. That mug's a weekend. This key is a month. Have you got anything bigger?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I lent her car to Jamie.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A month each, then. I used the key to let Jamie move into her flat.

cards.title: I Told You Enough
cards.instruction: Agree to be honest while repeatedly narrowing what honesty requires and which details count.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I put my pen down with yours. Account complete. I'll be honest: I took your donation box to the bank.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ran out of ink. Did you take the money inside it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, when I left. You didn't ask when.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Was it still in the box when you arrived?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At the car park, yes. If you mean the counter, that's a different arrival.

beats.text: You swiped the birthday photo away, so I did the same on my phone. Deleted. I'll be honest: I was eating dinner alone when you rang.

beats.text: That just closes the preview. Your brother's in our kitchen.

beats.text: Carving isn't eating. I meant the moments when food was actually in my mouth.

cards.title: The Conspiracy Expands
cards.instruction: Use every denial, coincidence, and missing detail as proof that more people and higher stakes are involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put gloves on, so I have too. You're right: protect the evidence. Our toaster receipt's gone; the shop must have someone inside this house.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm washing up. I probably recycled the receipt; we can get a copy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Washing up first, yes. So the recycling crew removes originals while the shop prints replacements.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Every shop prints replacement receipts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Every shop? Then it's the whole high street. We can't trust a single warranty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've folded my arms like you. I can keep a secret too. Tell me who asked you and your manager to match stories about my cancelled train.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm cold. The signal failed; it's on the public departure board.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep warm, yes. They've recruited the board operators to stop me reaching the interview.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The same fault is delaying three counties.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three counties to keep me unemployed. My replacement must already have government backing.

cards.title: Help Me Make This Normal
cards.instruction: Get someone to help perform the strange behavior until it feels ordinary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've raised my glass to the cupboard like you. Introductions done. Pass our talking guest a napkin.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was drinking water. And the cupboard hasn't got a lap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Drinks, then linen, of course. Put the napkin beside its handle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Should I offer it soup?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please. Ask which shelf it eats from.

beats.text: You put a cushion on the chair, so I added one. Our invisible dinner guest will be comfortable. Will you introduce Mum?
